criteria.note: plugin/templates/.github/workflows/warp-gate.yml parses as valid YAML (yaml.safe_load, 5 steps). The two gate steps invoke the REAL commands, not reimplementations: step 'Run the canonical gate' runs ./scripts/verify.sh and step 'Run the policy check' runs python3 .warp/policy_check.py. Checkout uses fetch-depth: 0, which policy_check's push_range/parent logic (head(), push_range_commits) genuinely needs to resolve server-side. Ran the exact sequence: verify.sh -> GATE GREEN (5 run, 18 na, 0 undeclared); policy_check.py -> exit 1 with its standard 'no passing independent verdict bound to HEAD' message, which is the gate correctly blocking (no verdict exists yet), i.e. it behaves as a server-side gate. Attack on selftest: verify.sh line 19 sets CHECK_unit=required:python3 scripts/selftest.py, so CI runs selftest THROUGH verify.sh; a separate selftest step would be redundant, not missing. Coverage is not dropped or weakened in CI.

Workflow carries ZERO company/product references (grep for bcengi|travelpass|workpass|dejitech|tripdesk|agentpass|coreconnect|companion|mvne returns nothing); 'Bcengi/warp' does not even appear in the workflow. verify.sh GATE GREEN at 14c7dab includes docs-hygiene (dash/non-ASCII/genericity), secret scan, and lint, all passing unchanged.

docs/plugin.md section 4.1 'Enforcing the same gate server-side' is proportionate: it states the CI check (verify.sh + policy_check.py), a 3-step required-status-check/branch-protection recipe that makes a failing policy_check unmergeable, and how it mirrors the local pre-push guard (policy_check is 'precisely what the guard's third stage runs'). The plugin contents tree lists the new template (.github/workflows/ warp-gate.yml). Honesty holds: the doc explicitly says 'Shipping the workflow does not by itself block a bad merge; making it a required status check does. That step is a host setting the repository owner applies once, and the plugin cannot apply it for you' and 'never something the repository self-enforces'. Unmergeability is correctly CONDITIONED on the human applying branch protection, not overstated. 9 server-side/branch-protection/required-status references; docs-hygiene green.

This is the crux and it is honest. .warp/capabilities.yaml and plugin/templates/.warp/capabilities.yaml are byte-identical (md5 b73980637f3a85e0c8635f78bf4dcb3c, matching the manifest's truncated claim). The prior server_side_enforcement=absent entry is GONE, replaced by two honest entries: ci_gate_check {status: reference, note: '...ships the artifact and does not self-configure the host'} and branch_protection_recipe {status: procedure, note: '...a host setting the repository owner applies once... the plugin cannot self-enforce it'}. Per the file's own vocabulary, reference = shipped reference impl wired per repo, procedure = human/agent-instructed and NOT enforced. NEITHER claims mechanical/automatic server-side self-enforcement. The danger (overclaiming mechanical enforcement that does not exist) is absent.

findings.text: The one non-ASCII character in W10's added lines is a box-drawing tree glyph in the docs/plugin.md plugin-contents tree. It is the pre-existing convention in that file and is explicitly allowed by scripts/check_docs.sh's non-ASCII sweep (whitelist includes U+2500-257F). Not a hygiene violation. No em-dash, en-dash, or double-hyphen separator anywhere in the diff; '--upgrade' is a legitimate pip flag and '---' occurrences are YAML front-matter delimiters.

PyYAML safe_load reports the 'on:' trigger key as the boolean True (a YAML 1.1 quirk shared by essentially every GitHub Actions workflow). Non-issue: GitHub Actions uses its own parser and reads 'on:' correctly; the trigger block (pull_request + push to main) is present and valid.

summary: All 4 ACs confirmed under adversarial review. The CI template invokes the REAL canonical commands (verify.sh, whose unit slot IS selftest.py, then policy_check.py) with fetch-depth: 0, reimplementing nothing and dropping no coverage; ran the exact sequence and verify.sh is GATE GREEN (0 undeclared) while policy_check correctly blocks absent a verdict. The template is fully generic (zero company/product references; Bcengi/warp not present). Docs section 4.1 gives a proportionate, honestly-conditioned branch-protection recipe that does not overstate unmergeability. The capabilities crux is clean: the absent entry is replaced by reference (shipped artifact) + procedure (human host setting) with NO overclaim of mechanical self-enforcement; both capability copies are byte-identical. Integrity: selftest 121 passed, none of the seven protected paths touched (no approval needed), change is additive/back-compat. Independently recomputed proof_digest = sha256:952aacf1babcafe0, matching the manifest. No blocking findings.
